questions.question: Where should hazardous materials be loaded and unloaded?
questions.explanation: Heat can make many hazardous materials more dangerous. Always load and unload hazardous materials away from heat sources.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how are they told apart?

options.text: The hazardous materials are listed first.
The non-hazardous materials are written in pencil.
The hazardous materials are written in red ink.
The hazardous materials are written larger than non-hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazardous materials are listed first.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must be shown differently from non-hazardous materials. They can be listed first, highlighted in a different color, or marked with an "X" in a column titled "HM."

questions.question: If a vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, what should the driver do?

options.text: Not warn others of the danger.
Keep the explosives in the vehicle until after the vehicles are separated.
Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, warn others and keep people away. Do not allow smoking or open fires. Remove the explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any buildings before separating the vehicles.

questions.question: What is a portable tank?

options.text: A tank that cannot be removed from a vehicle.
A tank that is not permanently attached to a vehicle.
A tank that is permanently attached to a vehicle.
A tank that should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: A tank that is not permanently attached to a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Portable tanks are bulk containers that can be removed from a vehicle. Cargo tanks stay on a vehicle at all times, whether they carry cargo or not.

questions.question: When sitting in the driver's seat, where should shipping papers be kept?
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers where you can reach them easily while wearing your seat belt. A pouch on the driver's door is a good location. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: If a substance is transported in a reportable quantity, what letters appear on the shipping paper and package?
questions.explanation: When a substance is transported in a reportable quantity, the letters "RQ" must be shown on the shipping paper and package.

questions.question: A person loading a hazardous materials tank must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stand within 10 feet of the tank.
Understand the hazards of the materials.
Be authorized to move the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stand within 10 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A supervisor watching the loading or unloading must be alert, able to see the tank clearly, and stand within 25 feet of it (not 10 feet). They must know the material hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if you need to run the engine to operate a pump.

questions.question: Who controls hazardous materials transportation laws?
questions.explanation: Because hazardous materials are dangerous, all levels of government—federal, state, and local—can make rules about how they are transported.

questions.question: How many classes of hazardous materials are there?
questions.explanation: There are nine classes of hazardous materials. Each class shows the type of danger the material presents.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tires with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check your tire pressure before each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only reliable way to check if your tires have the correct pressure.

questions.question: When loading a tank with flammable liquids, you should:

options.text: Connect a ground before opening the filling hole.
Connect a ground right before opening the filling hole.
Lock the filling hole while loading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect a ground before opening the filling hole.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. Connect a ground to the tank before opening the filling hole. Keep the ground connected until after you close the filling hole.

questions.question: ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle transporting hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials placards are required, place them on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: If transporting chlorine, what must be in the vehicle?

options.text: A phone with emergency numbers saved.

questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must have an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in their vehicle.

questions.question: Which location is NOT acceptable for keeping hazardous materials shipping papers?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while wearing a seat belt.
On the driver's seat when the driver is outside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: When driving, keep hazardous materials shipping papers on the driver's door or in a place the driver can see and reach easily. When the driver is outside the vehicle, keep the papers on the driver's seat.

questions.question: Shipping papers must list:

options.text: Fire department locations along the route.

questions.explanation: Shippers must list an emergency response telephone number on hazardous materials shipping papers. There are some exceptions to this rule.

questions.question: To drive a vehicle transporting hazardous materials, you must have:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a passenger endorsement.
A CDL with an air brake endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials, even if it is not carrying them at the time.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is to:
questions.explanation: The manual has all the information needed to pass the hazardous materials endorsement test, but not everything needed to do the job safely. Hazardous materials training courses provide additional important information.

questions.question: In the Hazardous Materials Table, Column 2 lists:
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table shows the correct shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: Class 7 hazardous materials are:
questions.explanation: Class 7 hazardous materials are radioactive materials.

questions.question: What should you do when loading or unloading explosive materials?

options.text: Use sharp-pointed tools to open the packages.

questions.explanation: Turn off your vehicle's engine before loading or unloading explosive materials. Never drop, throw, or roll packages containing explosives.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
The amount of packaging required for the shipment.
Where items can be placed on the trailer.
How the material should be loaded and unloaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: There are nine different hazard classes. A material's hazard class shows what risks it has.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, what are they certifying?

options.text: The package does not contain hazardous materials.
The package has been prepared according to the rules.
The package was packed at a specific location.
The package will be placed on the trailer first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The package has been prepared according to the rules.
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they confirm that the package has been prepared following all required rules.

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery. After delivery, turn off the engine ____ unhooking the hoses.
questions.explanation: If your engine runs a pump for product transfer, turn it off after the product transfer but before unhooking the hoses.

questions.question: What can you do with a vehicle that does not have the correct placards?

options.text: It can only be moved in an emergency.
It can be driven short distances.
It can be driven if it does not contain radioactive materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials must have the correct placards to be driven. An improperly placarded vehicle may only be driven if necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: Which one is not a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: A shipping paper describes hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers. Directions are not.

questions.question: If cargo containing hazardous materials is leaking, what should the driver do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to alert emergency personnel.
Drive to a designated hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel.
questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, do not drive any longer than necessary. Park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and send someone to get help. Continuing to drive would spread contamination.

questions.question: Who is responsible for putting placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Shippers provide the placards, but the driver is responsible for placing them on the vehicle.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.1 materials, what should the floor liner be made from?
questions.explanation: For Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials, use a tight floor liner made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron or iron alloys.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, how should you identify it?

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify the cargo.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, identify the materials using shipping papers, labels, or package location. Do not touch the leaking material.
